chat.title: OBD AI Assistant
chat.subtitle: Ask about your vehicle — diagnostics, error codes, live sensor data.
chat.quickPrompt0: What error codes do we have?
chat.quickPrompt2: Why is the engine heating up?
chat.noLiveDataBody: No adapter connected — answers come from general knowledge, not your car.
chat.simulatedDataBody: Readings come from a test adapter, not your car.
chat.gateBody: The assistant answers about your vehicle — its codes, sensors and readings. Connect an OBD-II adapter and it will have something to read.
chat.helpWhatBody: A conversation about this particular car. The assistant is joined to your adapter, so while you talk it can read live values, stored trouble codes, freeze-frame data and the VIN straight off the ECU.
chat.helpReadsTitle: It reads, it does not guess
chat.helpReadsBody: When an answer needs a number, the assistant asks the car for it and shows which reading it used. If the car cannot supply it, it says so instead of filling the gap — that is why an adapter has to be connected before this screen will open.
chat.helpAskBody: Plain questions work best: why the engine light is on, whether the coolant temperature is normal, what a code means on this make, or what a noise might be. Say what you noticed and when — the assistant pairs it with what the car reports.
chat.helpSessionsBody: Each conversation is a session and is kept. Start a fresh one with +, and open earlier ones with the clock. Sessions are deleted from that list.
chat.helpWriteBody: Reading is free, but anything that writes to the car — clearing trouble codes, for instance — is put to you first and only happens if you confirm it.
chat.helpLimitBody: The assistant only knows what the ECU reports. A fault the car has not detected is invisible to it, and a code names a symptom rather than the part to replace. Treat the answers as a starting point for a mechanic, not a replacement for one.

thresholds.subtitle: Alerts fire when a value crosses its threshold. Settings are saved per vehicle.
thresholds.coolantTempDesc: Alert when engine coolant exceeds this temperature.
thresholds.batteryVoltageDesc: Alert when control module voltage drops below this level.
thresholds.fuelLevelDesc: Alert when fuel tank level drops below this percentage.
thresholds.resetConfirmMessage: Restore all thresholds to their default values?
thresholds.outOfRange: Out of the usual range — check the value
thresholds.coolantRange: Most engines run 90–105 °C. Above 110 °C is overheating.
thresholds.batteryRange: A healthy battery rests at 12.4–12.7 V; charging reads 13.7–14.7 V.
thresholds.fuelRange: Set this to how much warning you want before the tank runs low.

pair.title: Connect Adapter
pair.intro: Pick a transport. Try each — the right one depends on your hardware.
pair.demoModeHint: Mock adapter — simulated PIDs, no hardware required
pair.noBleHint: Most cheap ELM327 clones use Bluetooth Classic. Try the BT Classic tab if nothing shows up here.
pair.classicIosNote: Bluetooth Classic is only supported on Android. Use BLE or WiFi on iOS.
pair.pairFirst: Pair the adapter from Android Bluetooth settings first (PIN usually 1234 or 0000), then come back here.
pair.wifiHint: Connect the phone to the adapter's WiFi network first (e.g. WiFi_OBDII, no internet). Defaults work for most clones.
pair.errPermBody: Please grant Bluetooth permissions in Settings to scan for OBD adapters.
pair.errBtOffBody: Please enable Bluetooth to scan for OBD adapters.
pair.errInvalidBody: Enter a valid host and port (e.g. 192.168.0.10 / 35000).
pair.scanningHint: Keep the adapter plugged in and close to the phone.
pair.helpStep1Body: A 16-pin trapezoid socket, almost always under the dashboard on the driver's side — near the pedals, the fuse box, or behind a small cover.
pair.helpStep2Body: Push it in firmly until it seats. Its LED should light up.
pair.helpStep3Body: Key to ON, or press start without touching the brake. The engine does not need to run, but the ECU has to be powered or it will not answer.
pair.helpStep4Body: For BLE, tap Scan here — do not pair the adapter in iOS Settings, these connect inside the app. For Wi-Fi, join the adapter's own network in Settings first, then come back.
pair.helpTrouble1: Check the adapter's LED — no light means no power at the port.
pair.helpTrouble2: Some clones take 10–20 seconds after power-up before they advertise.
pair.helpTrouble3: If your adapter is Bluetooth Classic rather than BLE, it cannot be used on iPhone — Apple only allows MFi-certified accessories on that protocol.

codes.title: Trouble codes
codes.needsMake: Manufacturer-specific — the vehicle's make is needed to define it.
codes.noDefinition: No definition in the bundled database.
codes.noAdapterBody: Connect your OBD-II adapter first — trouble codes are read from the car's ECU.
codes.askPrompt: My car has stored trouble code {{code}}. What does it mean, what usually causes it, how serious is it, and what should I check first?
codes.helpWhatBody: The ECU runs self-tests while you drive. When one fails, it stores a code and usually lights the check-engine lamp. A code names the symptom the ECU saw — not the part to replace.
codes.helpStoredBody: A confirmed fault. The ECU saw it often enough to be sure.
codes.helpPendingBody: Seen once, not yet confirmed. It becomes stored if it happens again, or clears itself if it does not.
codes.helpPermanentBody: Cannot be erased with any scan tool. It clears only after the ECU's own tests pass, which makes it the honest answer to whether a repair actually worked.
codes.helpLettersBody: P is powertrain, B body, C chassis, U network. P0xxx and P2xxx mean the same on every make; P1xxx differs per manufacturer, which is why the make matters.
codes.helpClearBody: Erasing codes wipes the ECU's memory and resets its readiness monitors. The fault returns as soon as the ECU sees it again, and you lose the freeze-frame data that would have helped diagnose it.
codes.clearConfirmBody: This erases the ECU's fault memory and its freeze-frame data, and resets the readiness monitors. It does not repair anything — if the fault is still there, the code comes back. Permanent codes cannot be cleared this way.
codes.clearedBody: The ECU reported no remaining codes.
codes.clearedPartialBody: {{count}} code(s) are still reported after the clear — either the fault is still present or they are permanent codes.
codes.clearOneBody: OBD-II has no command for erasing one code. Clearing removes {{code}} together with every other stored code, all freeze-frame data, and resets the readiness monitors. It repairs nothing — if the fault is still there, the code comes back.
codes.helpSingleTitle: Why codes cannot be cleared one at a time
codes.helpSingleBody: The standard has a single clear command and it wipes everything: all stored and pending codes, every freeze-frame snapshot, and the readiness monitors. Selective clearing does not exist in OBD-II, so any app offering it is either clearing everything or not clearing at all.
